results.title: OPERATION HADIN KAI NEUTRALISES 16 ISWAP FIGHTERS, TARGETS TERRORIST LEADERS IN LAKE CHAD By: Zagazola Makama Troops of the Joint Task Force
results.description:
OPERATION HADIN KAI NEUTRALISES 16 ISWAP FIGHTERS, TARGETS TERRORIST LEADERS IN LAKE CHAD

By: Zagazola Makama

Troops of the Joint Task Force (North East), Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK), have neutralised 16 suspected Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) fighters during coordinated air and artillery strikes on three suspected terrorist locations in the Tunbunma area of the southern Lake Chad region.

Security sources told Zagazola Makama that the operation was conducted between 1 a.m. and 2 a.m. on Oct. 26, following intelligence reports indicating the presence of key terrorist leaders and fighters at the targeted locations.

The sources said the operation involved the coordinated deployment of air and ground weapon systems to strike the identified terrorist positions.

A preliminary battle damage assessment indicated that 16 suspected ISWAP fighters were neutralised across the three locations.

Among those reportedly killed was Abu Zubiru, described as an Arab national, alongside two associates identified as Baana Nglewa and Jindullah Sadiq.

The sources added that Abu Saleem, identified as the Wali of Tunbunma, sustained severe injuries alongside seven other suspected fighters during the strikes.

The operation represents another attempt by OPHK to disrupt ISWAP’s leadership structure, degrade its fighting capacity and destroy its operational enclaves within the Lake Chad Basin.

The Tunbunma area, situated within the Lake Chad theatre, remains strategically important to terrorist groups operating across the waterways and surrounding islands, where difficult terrain can complicate surveillance and ground operations.

The latest strikes underscore the continued reliance on intelligence-led operations and coordinated air and ground capabilities to target terrorist concentrations and deny insurgents safe havens.

Operation Hadin Kai has reiterated its commitment to sustaining offensive operations against terrorist elements until security and normalcy are restored across the North-East.

Members of the public have also been urged to provide timely and credible information to security agencies to support ongoing counter-terrorism efforts.

results.title: BREAKING UPDATE Passengers travelling from Yauri in Kebbi State to Abuja were reportedly kidnapped by bandits yesterday, along with the driv
results.description:
BREAKING UPDATE
Passengers travelling from Yauri in Kebbi State to Abuja were reportedly kidnapped by bandits yesterday, along with the driver of the vehicle.
According to accounts and a video circulating online, one of the victims was seen speaking with their mother on the phone while an armed man pointed a rifle at the group. The number of people abducted is said to be more than ten.
No official confirmation or statement has been released yet. More details as they come.

results.title: Armed Bandits Reportedly Attacked Gidan Sarki Near Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto, Shooting a Cattle Owner and Stealing Dozens of Cows.
results.description:
Armed Bandits Reportedly Attacked Gidan Sarki Near Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto, Shooting a Cattle Owner and Stealing Dozens of Cows. 

SOKOTO, NIGERIA | Armed bandits have invaded Gidan Sarki, a community near the Faculty of Law of Usmanu Danfodiyo University, Sokoto (UDUS), shooting a cattle owner in the leg and rustling dozens of cows.

The attack reportedly occurred around 9 p.m. on Sunday, throwing residents into panic as the assailants arrived in the community and opened fire.

According to residents’ accounts, the attackers allegedly threatened members of the community and demanded that they bring out students living in the area.

results.title: TROOPS RESCUE THREE KIDNAPPED VICTIMS IN KEBBI By: Zagazola Makama Troops of the Nigerian Army, in collaboration with other security operati
results.description:
TROOPS RESCUE THREE KIDNAPPED VICTIMS IN KEBBI

By: Zagazola Makama

Troops of the Nigerian Army, in collaboration with other security operatives, have rescued three kidnapped victims during a joint fighting patrol in Sakaba Local Government Area of Kebbi State.

Security sources told Zagazola Makama that the operation was conducted at about 10:20 a.m. on Oct. 22 by troops of 223 Battalion, working alongside CT 10 and CIB III, from Dirindaji.

The sources said the joint team conducted a fighting patrol to Makuku and Dankolo villages, where the three victims were successfully rescued.

Following their rescue, the victims were handed over to the District Head of Dirindaji for further action.

results.description:
TROOPS ARREST SUSPECTED ISWAP COLLABORATOR OVER FORCED LEVIES IN YOBE

By: Zagazola Makama

Troops of the Nigerian Army, in collaboration with the Civilian Joint Task Force (CJTF), have arrested a suspected Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) collaborator at Geidam Market in Geidam Local Government Area of Yobe State.

Security sources told Zagazola Makama that the suspect was apprehended at about 1:30 p.m. on Oct. 24 while in possession of a mini truck.

The sources said preliminary interrogation revealed that the suspect allegedly confessed to actively receiving and delivering proceeds from forced levies imposed on local residents by terrorists.

Items recovered from the suspect included one mobile phone, a lighter and the sum of ₦18,450 in cash.

The suspect is currently in the custody of the troops for further investigation and necessary action.

The arrest is significant amid ongoing efforts by security forces to disrupt the financial and logistical networks sustaining terrorist activities in the North-East.

The collection of forced levies from residents and the subsequent movement of the proceeds are among the methods used by terrorist groups to generate funds and sustain their operations.

Security forces continue to intensify intelligence-led operations to identify individuals suspected of facilitating terrorist financing, logistics and other support activities across the region.

results.description: Other groups operating in Nigeria include Ansaru (al-Qaeda affiliate, active in northwest/central areas with kidnappings), Lakurawa (jihadist network linked to Sahel groups in Sokoto/Kebbi), and the Mahmuda group (near Kainji National Park). results.title: There is a part of Zamfara where armed groups are no longer behaving like ordinary criminals.
results.description:
There is a part of Zamfara where armed groups are no longer behaving like ordinary criminals.

They are acting like parallel governments.

They impose levies.

They decide who can mine.

They punish communities.

They block roads.

They plant explosives.

They demand compensation.

And ordinary villagers are trapped in the middle.

Premium Times reported that on October 5, terrorist leader Dankarami Gwaska and his fighters attacked a military base and mining sites around Bindin in Dansadau Emirate, Maru LGA.

Fourteen soldiers and mobile police officers were reportedly killed, and the armoury was looted.

The next day, Gwaska allegedly demanded compensation from nearby communities over weapons he said were lost when some of his fighters were killed.

Then came another level of terror.

Residents said his group imposed a ₦50 million “protection levy” on Bindin and neighbouring farming communities.

Within about two weeks, residents and security sources told Premium Times that roughly ₦360 million had been extorted from communities in the area.

Read that again.

Citizens living inside Nigeria were reportedly paying armed groups for the privilege of surviving in their own communities.

That is not just insecurity.

That is the erosion of state authority.

The situation became even more disturbing around the mining sites.

Premium Times reported that Gwaska’s group had struck arrangements with local miners, demanding a share of revenue from gold extraction while controlling access to strategic mining locations.

This is where the conversation about banditry must change.

It is no longer enough to talk only about kidnapping and cattle rustling.

Follow the money.

Gold.

Mining revenue.

Protection levies.

Ransom.

Illegal taxation.

Road control.

Weapons.

These are the economic engines that allow armed groups to survive.

And ordinary communities pay the price.

Another terrorist leader known as Rambo reportedly demanded the return of weapons seized by vigilantes and threatened communities after some of his men were killed.

His fighters allegedly attacked vulnerable settlements, blocked the Magami–Dansadau highway and planted improvised explosive devices on the road.

The military later cleared the explosives.

But a day after that operation, his men reportedly ambushed a civilian convoy travelling under military escort, killing travellers and burning vehicles.

This is the real tragedy.

Security forces strike terrorists.

Vigilantes strike terrorists.

Rival gangs fight terrorists.

Then the terrorists retaliate against villagers.

Who pays?

The farmer.

The trader.

The miner.

The woman travelling to market.

The family trying to return home.

That is why any serious security strategy must place civilian protection at its centre.

Killing terrorists is necessary.

But what happens to the villages they may retaliate against afterward?

Is intelligence immediately deployed?

Are vulnerable communities evacuated?

Are roads secured?

Are military posts reinforced?

Are civilians warned?

Are emergency response teams positioned nearby?

Because if every successful operation is followed by revenge attacks on unprotected communities, the state may win a tactical battle while civilians lose the war.

There is also an economic dimension government cannot ignore.

Zamfara’s gold-rich areas cannot be allowed to become private revenue territories for armed groups.

Every illegal mining network that finances terrorists should be mapped.

Every financier should be investigated.

Every gold buyer should be traceable.

Every supply chain should be scrutinised.

Because if armed groups can tax mining, extort communities and control roads, then they are funding their own violence.

Zamfara State itself recently asked for stronger federal intervention as attacks escalated, saying farming, trading and daily life in rural communities were being badly disrupted.

That request deserves urgency.

Not another ceremonial visit.

results.title: 🚨 ZAMFARA: VIGILANTES, CJTF REPEL BANDIT ASSAULT WITH AIR SUPPORT; OVER 30 SUSPECTED BANDITS REPORTEDLY KILLED A major security confrontatio
results.description:
🚨 ZAMFARA: VIGILANTES, CJTF REPEL BANDIT ASSAULT WITH AIR SUPPORT; OVER 30 SUSPECTED BANDITS REPORTEDLY KILLED

A major security confrontation in Birnin Tudu, Gummi LGA, Zamfara State, has reportedly left over 30 suspected bandits dead after local vigilantes and Civilian Joint Task Force (CJTF) members, backed by air support from Operation Fansan Yamma, resisted a sustained armed incursion.

But despite the reported retreat of the attackers, the security situation remains concerning.

HOW THE CONFRONTATION UNFOLDED

Preliminary reports indicate that the incident followed intelligence warnings about a large bandit movement from the northern direction towards the Bukkuyum axis. More than 59 motorcycles were reportedly sighted during the initial approach, raising concerns over the scale of the impending assault.

The attackers allegedly advanced through surrounding settlements, opened fire, looted shops and attempted to move livestock before engaging local defenders around Birnin Tudu.

Despite reportedly being outnumbered and inadequately equipped, community vigilantes, including members of the Yan Sakai network, alongside the CJTF, mounted resistance.

The intervention of air support reportedly increased pressure on the armed group, forcing elements of the attackers to withdraw and disperse into surrounding forests and rural routes.

CASUALTIES AND A CONCERNING WITHDRAWAL PATTERN

Local accounts put the number of suspected bandits killed at over 30, although the casualty figure remains unverified. At least five civilians were also reportedly killed in separate attacks, while several residents sustained injuries.

The attackers were subsequently reported moving towards the Tsallaken Gulbin–Nasarawa Kifi area, with other elements allegedly dispersing towards Zauma and Yan Gizazza.

Separate reports of a convoy involving more than 150 motorcycles have also emerged. However, it remains unclear whether this movement involved the same group engaged at Birnin Tudu or a separate armed element.

THE WIDER SECURITY IMPLICATIONS

The confrontation follows reports of attacks on Tudu and Daki Takwas, during which approximately 1,000 cattle and residents’ motorcycles were allegedly stolen.

Beyond the reported casualties, the livestock losses pose a serious economic threat to farming and pastoral households already affected by persistent insecurity.

Vigilante commander Bello Abubakar, popularly known as Bello Karo Birnin Tudu, has appealed for additional security personnel, an armoured vehicle, weapons, ammunition and other operational equipment. He also warned of a possible reprisal attack.

While the reported resistance may have disrupted the attackers’ immediate objective, their dispersal across multiple routes presents a continuing security concern. The possibility of regrouping, renewed attacks or reprisals cannot be ruled out.

KEY QUESTION: Has the threat to Birnin Tudu been neutralised, or have the fleeing gunmen merely repositioned for another attack?

Monitoring continues. Casualty figures, the reported movements and the full extent of the operation require independent verification.

Credit:@ZagazOlaMakama
